title: A Timeline of Mumbai Indians’s Home-Ground Evolution
dek: Wankhede has changed around Mumbai Indians: in scores, in the balance between bat and ball, and in how often the home side wins.
excerpt: First-innings scores at Wankhede have moved between the early seasons and the latest ones, and Mumbai Indians' home record has moved with them. The ground's evolution is part of the franchise's story.

sections.heading: A Ground That Changes
body: Pitches are relaid, boundaries move, and the league's batting changes around them. A home ground's character is not fixed.
At Wankhede, the average first-innings score was {{ev:he-early}} in {{ev:he-early-y}} and {{ev:he-late}} in {{ev:he-late-y}}. The chart shows every season with at least three matches at the ground.

sections.heading: The Home Record Through Time
body: Mumbai Indians won {{ev:he-w1}} of their decided home matches in 2008–2023 and {{ev:he-w2}} since 2024.
A changing ground can help or hurt a home side, depending on whether the squad is built for the new conditions.

sections.heading: Ground or League?
body: Part of the rise in scores at any ground reflects the league-wide rise in scoring, especially since the impact-player rule arrived in 2023.

sections.heading: What the Data Does Not Record
body: The warehouse does not record pitch preparation, boundary dimensions or renovations, so the reasons for changes at the ground cannot be read from it.
Those would come from ground records and curators.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Build for the Ground as It Is Now
body: Wankhede today is not the ground of the early seasons. Mumbai Indians' squad should be built for the conditions in the latest seasons, not the historical ones.
The home-ground articles elsewhere in this series measure today's conditions in more detail.
